issue.standard_remedy: Map the sub-tier and qualify an alternate
issue.summary: Depends on a single-source sub-tier supplier (North America)

plan.diagnosis: Atlas Metals presents a single-source sub-tier dependency risk with USD 1,459,305 in trailing 12-month spend and a low resiliency score of 49 out of 100. The supplier experienced 1 disruption event in the past 12 months and relies on 30 sub-tier suppliers, creating significant supply chain vulnerability despite North America geographic location.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct sub-tier mapping exercise with Atlas Metals to identify the critical single-source sub-tier supplier(s) and obtain full visibility into the 30 sub-tier dependencies
Issue RFI to 3-5 alternative metal suppliers with comparable capabilities to assess dual-sourcing feasibility and obtain budgetary pricing for the USD 1,459,305 annual spend
Negotiate contractual transparency clause with Atlas Metals requiring 90-day advance notice of sub-tier changes and quarterly sub-tier risk reporting
Qualify and onboard one backup supplier for 20-30% of volume (USD 291,861 to 437,792) to establish dual-source position
Implement safety stock buffer equal to 4-6 weeks of demand for critical metal components sourced through Atlas Metals

plan.expected_impact: Mitigate supply disruption risk on USD 1,459,305 annual spend and improve resiliency score from 49 to target of 70+ through dual-sourcing strategy covering 20-30% of volume (USD 291,861 to 437,792).
kpis: Dual-source coverage achieving 20-30% of USD 1,459,305 spend within 6 months
Sub-tier visibility: 100% mapping of 30 sub-tier suppliers
Disruption event reduction from 1 to 0 over next 12 months
Safety stock days of supply: maintain 28-42 days for critical SKUs
risks: Atlas Metals may resist sub-tier transparency requirements, delaying mapping exercise
Alternative supplier qualification may exceed 16-week timeline due to technical specifications or quality testing requirements
Dual-sourcing may increase total cost by 3-8% due to volume split and loss of economies of scale on USD 1,459,305 spend
Safety stock buffer will increase working capital requirements by approximately USD 112,254 to 168,381 (4-6 weeks of USD 1,459,305 annual spend)
Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite and Coupa configurations may not synchronize supplier updates consistently across multi-ERP environment
erp_actions: SAP: Add second source to material master source list (ME01) for all Atlas Metals part numbers with quota arrangement 70/30 split
SAP: Update LFM1 purchasing organization data to flag Atlas Metals with 'Sub-tier Risk' in vendor master field ZSUBTIER_RISK
Oracle EBS: Create supplier site attribute to track resiliency score (49) and set review flag for annual reassessment
Coupa: Enable supplier risk monitoring workflow to require quarterly sub-tier attestation from Atlas Metals
NetSuite: Configure safety stock levels to 4-6 weeks demand for all items sourced from Atlas Metals (vendor ID)
Dynamics 365: Add alternate vendor associations for dual-source setup and update procurement policies to require split POs above USD 50,000
All ERPs: Create spend alert threshold at USD 1,459,305 annual run-rate to flag concentration risk if single-source volume increases
